name: Amcor

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Amcor logo.svg, vector from Amcor brand assets); Wikipedia infobox PNG is only 248 px

description: Amcor makes the plastic, aluminum and paper film pouches, bottles, jars and closures that wrap food, drinks, medicines and personal-care products, selling to consumer-goods and healthcare companies around the world. It sells through a direct sales force to thousands of customers, none above 10% of sales, and passes resin and film cost changes through to customers by contract over time. The April 30, 2025 merger with Berry Global lifted net sales from $15.0B in FY2025 to $23.5B in FY2026 and roughly doubled the rigid packaging business. Debt was $14.0B at June 30, 2026, and a 1-for-5 reverse share split took effect January 14, 2026.

businessLines.name: Global Flexible Packaging Solutions
businessLines.how: Per-unit sales of custom-printed packaging to consumer-goods and medical customers on multi-year supply relationships, with raw-material (resin, aluminum) cost passed through by contract mechanisms.
businessLines.description: Flexible packaging (films, pouches, lidding, labels) in polymer resin, aluminum and fiber for food, beverage, healthcare and other products; about 36,000 employees at about 190 facilities in 33 countries.

businessLines.name: Global Rigid Packaging Solutions
businessLines.how: Per-unit sales of molded containers and closures to beverage, food, personal-care and pharma customers; resin cost passed through by contract.
businessLines.description: Rigid containers, closures, dispensing and pharma delivery devices (bottles, jars, closures, dispensers); about 38,000 employees at about 210 facilities in 33 countries; roughly doubled by the Berry merger.

brands.name: Berry Global Group, Inc. (merged 2025-04-30)
brands.share: Folded into both segments; 10-K gives no separate Berry revenue. FY2026 net sales rose to $23,506M from $15,009M.
